name: core
purpose: Reusable lessons that fix image prompts. Each lesson is one sentence and one fix. Lessons with wins climb. Lessons that keep failing retire.

lessons.title: Say one job per prompt
lessons.trigger: prompt does three or more things
lessons.instruction: Give the image one job. If you want a new background, new light and new text, run three passes and keep the best of each.
lessons.evidence: Three merged asks produced a muddy result in 4 of 5 tests.

lessons.title: Quote the exact text
lessons.instruction: List every on-image string in its own block, in quotes, and say copy it character by character. Never bury text inside a sentence.
lessons.evidence: Separate text lists fixed invented words in every poster test.

lessons.title: Never paste raw JSON
lessons.instruction: Read the JSON and write plain labeled sentences. Braces, quotes and key names can be painted into the picture as visible text.
lessons.evidence: Raw JSON blobs leaked 'blocks' and 'task' into posters.

lessons.title: Name the empty space
lessons.instruction: Reserve space as a named area: 'the left third stays empty'. Vague 'leave room for text' centers the subject instead.
lessons.evidence: Naming a third fixed crowding in 4 of 4 thumbnail runs.

lessons.title: Put the phone test in the prompt
lessons.instruction: Write the viewing size into the task: 'readable on a phone at 160 pixels wide'. The model then sizes and spaces type for that size.
lessons.evidence: Adding the size test reduced tiny-text failures to near zero.

lessons.title: Lock the thing that must not change
lessons.trigger: editing a real photo or product
lessons.instruction: Write one line per locked feature: face, label spelling, logo shape, proportions. Unlocked features drift first.
lessons.evidence: Explicit locks stopped label redesign in product tests.

lessons.title: Ban beautification by name
lessons.instruction: Add: do not smooth skin, slim faces or change age. The default edit direction makes people look like different people.
lessons.evidence: Faces stayed recognizable after adding the ban.

lessons.title: Ask for a contact shadow
lessons.instruction: Add 'soft contact shadow under the base'. Without it the object floats and the image reads as fake.
lessons.evidence: Floating-product complaints vanished in catalog tests.

lessons.title: Three references, three jobs
lessons.instruction: Use one reference for face, one for outfit, one for style. More images blur which signal wins.
lessons.evidence: Five-reference runs showed style drift; three-reference runs held.

lessons.title: Test at 1K, deliver at 2K or 4K
lessons.instruction: Run ideas at 1K. Re-run only the winner at 2K or 4K. 1K and 2K bill the same, so 2K is the safe delivery tier.
lessons.evidence: Testing at 1K cut spend per accepted image in half.

lessons.title: Flat page, not a photo of a page
lessons.instruction: Add 'no perspective, no shadows, no mockup device'. Otherwise you get a photo of a poster instead of a page you can post.
lessons.evidence: Removed mockup frames from every infographic run.

lessons.title: Numbers are the risk
lessons.instruction: Check every digit, date and currency at full zoom before sending. The model can invent a plausible number that nobody asked for.
lessons.evidence: Invented percentages appeared in 2 of 6 early infographics.

lessons.title: One language per image
lessons.instruction: Make a separate image per language and attach the first as the layout master. Mixed-language prompts leak glyphs.
lessons.evidence: Single-image bilingual tests produced wrong accents.

lessons.title: Say it as a want, not a ban
lessons.instruction: Replace 'no clutter' with 'empty background'. Image models follow positive descriptions more reliably than prohibitions.
lessons.evidence: Positive rewrites held up; long ban lists sometimes added the banned item.

lessons.title: Keep the grain
lessons.instruction: Add 'keep the original grain and texture'. Cleaned-up scans without grain look like renders, not photographs.
lessons.evidence: One confirmed restoration where grain kept the print believable.

lessons.title: Hands and eyes hide errors
lessons.instruction: Before saving, look at hands, eyes and small text at 100%. These three areas fail first and cost the most to reshoot.
lessons.evidence: Most rejected images failed on one of these three.

lessons.title: Keep prompts under 30 lines
lessons.instruction: Cap each prompt at about 30 lines. Past that, rules start competing and the model drops the ones at the end.
lessons.evidence: Long prompts lost their final instructions in 2 tests.

lessons.title: Old prompt that lost
lessons.instruction: Add a long list of camera settings to force realism.
lessons.evidence: Long lens lists added noise and rarely changed the result.
